# eslint-plugin-jwt-security

Guide for AI coding assistants using this plugin in a project. To change the plugin's own source, read https://github.com/ofri-peretz/eslint/blob/main/AGENTS.md instead.

> ESLint JWT security rules — detects algorithm confusion (CVE-2022-23540), alg:none, weak or hardcoded secrets, and decode-without-verify.

## Enable it

```bash
npm install --save-dev eslint-plugin-jwt-security
```

Requires ESLint ^8.40.0 || ^9.0.0 || ^10.0.0 and Node >=22.13.0.

Flat config files (`eslint.config.*`) are found by ESLint 8.57 and newer; on ESLint 9 and 10 they are the default.

```js
// eslint.config.mjs
import jwtSecurity from 'eslint-plugin-jwt-security';

export default [jwtSecurity.configs.recommended];
```

Each preset is one flat config object: put it in the array as an element, do not spread it. Rule ids are prefixed `jwt-security/`. Add it to the config you already have; do not remove other plugins. TypeScript files need a TypeScript parser in the config (`typescript-eslint`).

Use it alongside `eslint-plugin-security`, not instead of it: keep that plugin if the project has it. Measured overlap and the limits of both: https://eslint.interlace.tools/docs/getting-started/with-eslint-plugin-security

## Presets

| Preset        | Rules | Errors | Warnings |
| ------------- | ----- | ------ | -------- |
| `flagship`    | 1     | 1      | 0        |
| `recommended` | 10    | 8      | 2        |
| `strict`      | 13    | 13     | 0        |
| `legacy`      | 3     | 2      | 1        |
| `all`         | 13    | 13     | 0        |

### `flagship`

1 rule:

- `no-algorithm-none` (error): Disallow JWT "none" algorithm which bypasses signature verification (CVE-2022-23540).

### `recommended`

10 rules:

- `no-algorithm-none` (error): Disallow JWT "none" algorithm which bypasses signature verification (CVE-2022-23540).
- `no-algorithm-confusion` (error): Prevent algorithm confusion attacks using symmetric algorithms with asymmetric keys.
- `require-algorithm-whitelist` (error): Require explicit algorithm specification in JWT verify operations.
- `no-decode-without-verify` (error): Disallow trusting decoded JWT payload without signature verification.
- `no-weak-secret` (error): Require strong secrets (256+ bits) for HMAC-based JWT signing.
- `no-hardcoded-secret` (error): Disallow hardcoded secrets in JWT sign/verify operations.
- `no-timestamp-manipulation` (error): Prevent disabling automatic timestamp generation which enables replay attacks.
- `require-expiration` (error): Require expiration claim (exp) or expiresIn option in JWT signing.
- `no-sensitive-payload` (warn): Prevent storing sensitive data in JWT payload which is only base64-encoded.
- `require-issued-at` (warn): Require iat (issued at) claim for token freshness validation.

### `strict`

Everything in `recommended` plus 3 more (some shared rules run at a different severity here):

- `require-issuer-validation` (error): Require issuer (iss) claim validation in JWT verify operations.
- `require-audience-validation` (error): Require audience (aud) claim validation in JWT verify operations.
- `require-max-age` (error): Require maxAge option in verify operations to enforce token freshness.

### `legacy`

3 rules:

- `no-algorithm-none` (error): Disallow JWT "none" algorithm which bypasses signature verification (CVE-2022-23540).
- `no-algorithm-confusion` (error): Prevent algorithm confusion attacks using symmetric algorithms with asymmetric keys.
- `no-hardcoded-secret` (warn): Disallow hardcoded secrets in JWT sign/verify operations.

### `all`

Everything in `recommended` plus 3 more (some shared rules run at a different severity here):

- `require-issuer-validation` (error): Require issuer (iss) claim validation in JWT verify operations.
- `require-audience-validation` (error): Require audience (aud) claim validation in JWT verify operations.
- `require-max-age` (error): Require maxAge option in verify operations to enforce token freshness.

## Other Interlace plugins by dependency

If the project also depends on one of these, add the matching plugin the same way:

- `express`, `fastify`, `koa`, `@hapi/hapi`, `restify`, `hono`, `next`, `@nestjs/core`, `@nestjs/common`, `aws-lambda`, `@types/aws-lambda`, `@middy/core`, `commander`, `yargs`, `@oclif/core`, `@modelcontextprotocol/*`: `eslint-plugin-node-security`
- `express`: `eslint-plugin-express-security`
- `@nestjs/common`, `@nestjs/core`: `eslint-plugin-nestjs-security`
- `react`, `react-dom`, `preact`, `vue`, `svelte`, `@angular/core`, `solid-js`, `lit`, `next`, `nuxt`: `eslint-plugin-browser-security`
- `pg`, `pg-pool`, `pg-promise`, `postgres`, `slonik`: `eslint-plugin-postgresql-security`
- `mysql2`, `mysql`: `eslint-plugin-mysql-security`
- `mongodb`, `mongoose`: `eslint-plugin-mongodb-security`
- `better-sqlite3`, `sqlite3`: `eslint-plugin-sqlite-security`
- `knex`: `eslint-plugin-knex-security`
- `@prisma/client`, `prisma`: `eslint-plugin-prisma-security`
- `drizzle-orm`: `eslint-plugin-drizzle-security`
- `sequelize`: `eslint-plugin-sequelize-security`
- `typeorm`: `eslint-plugin-typeorm-security`
- `@supabase/supabase-js`: `eslint-plugin-supabase-security`
- `@grpc/reflection`, `grpc-server-reflection`: `eslint-plugin-grpc-security`
- `@modelcontextprotocol/*`: `eslint-plugin-mcp-sdk-security`
- `openai`, `@openai/agents`: `eslint-plugin-openai-security`
- `@anthropic-ai/sdk`, `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk`: `eslint-plugin-anthropic-security`
- `@google/genai`: `eslint-plugin-gemini-security`
- `ai`: `eslint-plugin-vercel-ai-security`
- `aws-lambda`, `@types/aws-lambda`, `@middy/core`: `eslint-plugin-lambda-security`

The full stack-to-plugin playbook (with config rendering and a proof step) is the `security-linting` skill: https://github.com/ofri-peretz/eslint/tree/main/skills/security-linting
